applies_when: deciding whether a task needs an agent, a workflow, or a single model call
building or changing an agent loop, its tools, or its context handling
splitting work across multiple agents

key_rules.rule: Build an agent only when the task passes all four gate criteria; otherwise use a single call or a workflow.
Key loop termination off the structured stop signal; keep the iteration cap as a backstop only.
Give each agent a narrow tool surface; do not give every agent every tool.
Give tools when-to-call descriptions, strict schemas, and structured errors.
Coordinate multiple agents through a task queue and structured shared state, never direct hand-offs.
Validate output at every hand-off and keep a rollback for bad outputs.

playbooks.title: Building AI Agents

applies_when: taking an agent or LLM feature to production
adding observability, cost controls, evals, or security to an agent
handling untrusted input or prompt injection in an agent

key_rules.rule: Start with the simplest thing and add autonomy only when it demonstrably improves outcomes.
Treat context as finite and degrading; curate it instead of filling it.
Instrument cost per task, not just accuracy.
Grade outcomes, not paths.
Contain at the environment layer first and steer at the model layer second.
Keep prompt and response content capture opt-in.

playbooks.title: Building Reliable Agents

applies_when: building or changing a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline
chunked documents lose context needed to retrieve them
deciding whether to add BM25, reranking, or full-context prompting

key_rules.rule: Test putting the whole knowledge base in a cached prompt before building retrieval when it is under 200,000 tokens.
Generate context from the complete document and one target chunk, and prepend it before both the embedding and BM25 indexes.
Build a local eval set before choosing the embedding model, fusion settings, chunk shape, or reranker.
Add reranking only when the quality gain justifies the added latency and cost.
Treat the published preprocessing cost as a dated estimate under stated assumptions.

playbooks.title: Contextual Retrieval

applies_when: granting an agent a new power such as merge, send, spend, or deploy
adding or removing a human approval gate
supervising agents takes more time than the work

key_rules.rule: Grant no agent full access on day one.
Record the autonomy level per action type, not one level per agent.
Start at L2 for critical operations and L3 for minor incidents.
Write measurable promotion criteria and wire automatic demotion to live risk signals.
Count approval clicks, re-prompts, and clean-up of agent output as toil.

playbooks.title: Autonomy and approval gates

applies_when: giving an agent a tool, credential, memory store, or external channel
an agent can write, spend, or reach outside systems

key_rules.rule: Keep authorization downstream of the model; a system prompt is not a control.
Give each agent its own short-lived, scoped credentials; no shared or developer credentials.
Cap tokens, cost, tool calls, wall-clock time, and delegation depth per task.
Dry-run mutating calls before production state changes.
Stop an agent with a circuit breaker after repeated consecutive failures.
Keep an emergency stop that pauses in-flight actions, blocks new ones, and revokes L3 permissions fleet-wide.

playbooks.title: Blast radius for agent tools

applies_when: monitoring production quality of an agent or AI feature
a model, prompt, tool, or input mix changes under a running system
trusting an old eval or a model judge

key_rules.rule: Do not trust a judge that has never been compared with human labels.
Offline evals alone do not detect drift.
Watch input mix, model version, tool errors, tokens per task, judge agreement, and calibration.
Tier labels as bronze, silver, and gold.
Read traces until you stop learning new failure types.

playbooks.title: Drift and silent quality decay

applies_when: an agent takes a harmful action or a group of agents stalls
a model provider fails during operation
an AI product gives harmful output

key_rules.rule: A human is the incident commander, never an agent.
Agents investigate read-only and propose; the incident commander decides.
Make every change through one actuation path with pre-flight checks.
Mitigate first; do not root-cause while damage continues.
Do not lose transcripts before analysis.

playbooks.title: Incident response for agent systems

applies_when: designing or launching an agent-backed product or feature
signing off reliability before build or before launch

key_rules.rule: Define the critical user journeys and what correct means for each.
Give every agent feature a fallback without the model.
Review SLOs, autonomy, blast radius, evals, tracing, drift, and incident roles together.
Keep a failure-mode table, a rollback, and degraded modes.
Design reliability in before launch; adding it later costs more.

playbooks.title: Launch review for agentic products

applies_when: adding tracing or metrics to an agent
computing reliability indicators from agent traces

key_rules.rule: Measure tasks, not spans.
Compute tool error rate from execute_tool spans with error.type set.
Include failed and retried attempts in tokens and cost per task.
Pin the GenAI and MCP convention version you implement and recheck it before an upgrade.
Do not let reliability data become a data-leak path.

playbooks.title: Observability: SLIs from traces

applies_when: writing up an agent incident or a notable bad output

key_rules.rule: Stay blameless for humans and agents alike.
Build the timeline from traces, not memory.
Classify each incident with one OWASP agentic risk category.
Add a regression eval case; a postmortem without one is incomplete.
Give every action item an owner.

playbooks.title: Postmortems for agent incidents

applies_when: changing a model, system prompt, skill, tool schema, or agent framework version

key_rules.rule: Version prompts, skills, model ids, tool schemas, and harness versions, and record each on every trace.
Gate each release per slice against the last known-good baseline.
Canary on one worker pool or a small share of traffic and compare SLIs per version.
Abort on quality regression even when infrastructure looks healthy.
Do not swap models in one big step.
Add incident cases to the eval set so it does not go stale.

playbooks.title: Eval-gated releases and canaries

applies_when: launching or reviewing an agent and defining how reliable it must be
choosing SLIs, SLO targets, error budgets, or burn-rate alerts
planning agent capacity, provider quotas, or cost

key_rules.rule: Uptime alone is not an SLO for an agent.
Use pass or fail indicators, not one-to-ten judge scores.
Set targets per consequence tier and alert on burn rate over two windows.
Count retries in cost.
Discover provider quotas in a load test, not in an incident.

playbooks.title: SLOs and error budgets for agents
